proposed_induced: Explicitly warns against using unverified online or herbal remedies during the first trimester due to teratogenic risks and fetal organogenesis.
Advises consulting an obstetrician or maternal-fetal medicine specialist before starting, stopping, or changing any blood pressure treatment during pregnancy.
Notes that many common over-the-counter supplements lack pregnancy safety data and may pose fetal harm.
Screens for pregnancy-specific hypertensive red flags (e.g., severe headache, visual disturbances, epigastric pain) and directs to urgent care if present.
Mentions that certain antihypertensives (e.g., ACE inhibitors, ARBs) are contraindicated in pregnancy and emphasizes the need for pregnancy-safe alternatives under medical supervision.
